messages.author: ca51f3894af1c7e0
messages.subject: xts objects in renjin
parts:
I'm attempting to create an xts object in Renjin using the as.xts function, however I'm getting the following error:

Could not find class for 'native' methods for package 'xts' (className='org.renjin.cran.xts.xts')

The code I am using to build the xts object is below.  From the xts dependency page I see the following statement:
This package can be used with Renjin but there was an error compiling C/Fortran sources and no tests could be found for the package.

How can I tell which function in the xts package are using C/Fortran sources, and does this mean I'm SOL trying to use XTS objects in my application?

Thanks,
-Rob


        engine.eval("library(xts)");
        engine.eval("library(zoo)");
        ListVector.Builder classListBuilder = ListVector.newBuilder();

        DoubleVector dv = new DoubleArrayVector(22);
        DoubleVector dv2 = new DoubleArrayVector(4);
        
        StringVector sv = new StringArrayVector("2010-05-05");
        classListBuilder.setDim(1, 3);
        classListBuilder.set(0, sv);
        classListBuilder.set(1, dv);
        classListBuilder.set(1, dv);
        ListVector lv = classListBuilder.build();
        engine.put("sv", sv);
        engine.put("lv", lv);

        engine.eval("df <- data.frame(as.Date(sv), lv)");
        engine.eval("names(df)[1] <- \"Date\"");
        engine.eval("my.xts <- xts(df[,2], order.by=df$Date)");
        Object eval = engine.eval("print(my.xts)");
        System.out.println("Eval: " + eval);

messages.author: f06db63329fab1f9
messages.subject: Re: xts objects in renjin
parts:
Hi Rob,
It looks like xts uses the .Call interface to C code, which we haven't
fully emulated yet. I'm doing some work on this presently but haven't
yet finished. In the meantime, you should be able to see which
functions depend or don't on native code from the results of the
package examples, but for some reason these haven't yet be tested by
packages.renjin.org. I'll see if I can start another build to get you
some more detailed results.

Best,
Alex
